The handler's `uniqueGuests` filter only removes guests already in booking.attendees or blacklisted — duplicates within the input array survive and are passed to `createMany`, persisting duplicate attendee rows, and sendAddGuestsEmails iterates attendees sending each duplicate an email. This is a server-side defect bypassable via direct API call.

judged_text: The server schema accepts duplicate emails in the guests array (no uniqueness refine and no case normalization), so a direct API call with ['a@x.com','a@x.com'] creates duplicate attendee rows via createMany. Duplicate attendee records are persisted and each duplicate receives its own copy of the ICS/notification email; the only uniqueness enforcement lives in the client-side dialog schema, which is trivially bypassed by any non-UI caller.

Duplicate attendee records are persisted and each duplicate receives its own copy of the ICS/notification email; the only uniqueness enforcement lives in the client-side dialog schema, which is trivially bypassed by any non-UI caller.

adjudication.rationale: The server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema only validates email format (z.array(z.string().email())) and does not enforce uniqueness or normalize case. In addGuests.handler.ts, `uniqueGuests` filters only against *existing* `booking.attendees` and the blacklist, not against duplicates within `guests`, so an input like ['a@x.com','a@x.com'] will produce duplicate entries in `guestsFullDetails` and be persisted via `attendees.createMany`. Additionally, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` uses the original (possibly duplicated) `guests`, and the event’s attendees list can include duplicates, causing multiple notification/ICS emails to the same address. Client-side uniqueness refine in AddGuestsDialog is bypassable by direct API calls.
